findings.body:
Removal of the `ALLOWED_HOSTS` check means `deliver(event, url)` now performs an HTTP POST to any URL the caller supplies. If this function is reachable with untrusted `url` values (customer webhook endpoints), an attacker can exfiltrate data or cause SSRF.

```suggestion
def deliver(event: dict, url: str) -> int:
    host = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname or ""
    if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS:
        raise ValueError("webhook host not allowed")
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json_dumps(event), method="POST")
```
`json_dumps` is referenced but never defined or imported. The only import remaining is `urllib.request`; every call to `deliver` will raise NameError.

summary: The change removes the only host allow-list and the hostname validation that enforced it. The resulting `deliver` function now performs `urllib.request.urlopen` against an arbitrary caller-supplied URL with no remaining controls. In addition, the code on the retained lines references an undefined name `json_dumps`. Both issues are visible on lines that appear in the diff.

verification.reason: The patch removes ALLOWED_HOSTS and the hostname check, so deliver() now urlopen-POSTs to any caller-supplied URL; the new comment explicitly allows customer endpoints, which is a real SSRF/exfiltration regression.
webhooks.py calls json_dumps(event) with only urllib.request imported and no definition of json_dumps anywhere in the repo, so deliver will raise NameError on every call.
